question.problem:
For the piecewise function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+x-1\, & \text{ for }\,x<2 \\ {x}^{2}+bx+3\, & \text{ for }\,x>2\end{aligned}
$$

it is known that ${lim}_{x\to 2}f(x)$ exists. What is the value of the constant $b?$
question.worked_solution:
In order for ${lim}_{x\to 2}f(x)$ to exist, the left and right-sided limits must both exist and be equal.

- Approaching from the left, we have $x<2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={x}^{2}+x-1.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}{x}^{2}+x-1 \\  & =(2)^{2}+2-1 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

- Approaching from the right, we have $x>2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={x}^{2}+bx+3.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}{x}^{2}+bx+3 \\  & =(2)^{2}+b\cdot 2+3 \\  & =7+2b.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the left and right-sided limits must be equal, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{+}}f(x) \\ 5 & =7+2b \\ 2b & =-2 \\ b & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
